title: Gradient Flow
one_sentence_summary: Gradient flow describes how learning signals propagate backward through a network.
quick_recall: Training depends on usable gradients reaching early layers; repeated transformations can shrink, explode, or distort them.
core_explanation: Backpropagation multiplies derivatives through a computational graph. Very deep paths can make the signal numerically or geometrically difficult to use. Short identity paths, careful initialization and normalization help preserve effective learning signals.
why_it_matters: Poor gradient flow makes optimization slow or prevents early layers from learning.
